newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Moslem official warns against Jerusalem project.
newsitem.headline: Moslem official warns against Jerusalem project.

text.p: A senior Moslem official in Arab East Jerusalem was quoted on Wednesday as saying that a proposed Israeli renovation project in the holy city would spark violence.

Israeli Religious Affairs Ministry spokesman Shimon Malka said on Tuesday officials had decided in February to look into refurbishing an area in the Moslem quarter to give Jewish worshippers better access to another part of the Old City's Western Wall, Judaism's holiest site.

Adnan al-Husseini, director of the Islamic Waqf department in Jerusalem said in remarks published by al-Ayyam newspaper that the proposed renovation site was a 500-year-old Mameluke building which was owned by Moslems.
"The said location is an Islamic site, 100 percent, and it is part of al-Aqsa mosque," Husseini was quoted as saying.
The site is located in an area of high Moslem population density, Husseini added.
The paper said Husseini warned the Israeli government against even considering infringing on the site saying such "thinking would be wrong and provocative".
"Those who stand behind it seek to stir anger and create problems and unrest," the paper quoted Husseini as saying.
Israel's opening of a tourist tunnel near al-Aqsa mosque in September set off gunbattles in which 61 Palestinians and 15 Israelis died.
Husseini said Israeli plans were dangerous and could ignite even worse violence than the September bloodshed.
Jerusalem is holy to Christians, Moslems and Jews. Israel captured East Jerusalem, including the Old City, in the 1967 Middle East war and later annexed it as its "indivisible" capital.
The PLO claims East Jerusalem as the capital of a future Palestinian state.
